transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood Solutions), Priya Rao (Lighthouse Orbit CTO), Marcus Flynn (Lighthouse Lead Infra), Aisha Khan (Lighthouse Partnerships), Tom (procurement)

Summary:
Quick partner discovery between Redwood and Lighthouse Orbit to understand integrator/onramp needs for hybrid SaaS + on-prem GPU deployments. Focus areas: VPC/private control plane requirements, pilot scope for connector (routing and KV cache), compliance & procurement timeline, and a plan for a short performance runbook.

Topics:
- Architectural constraints (air-gapped pockets, on-prem GPU pools)
- Security & compliance: SOC2/ISO, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML
- Integration patterns: API-only, sidecar agent, or marketplace connector
- Pilot success criteria and timeline

Action items (auto): see action_items field

Transcript:
[00:00:12] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Sounds like we have a full table, I'll do a super quick intro to Redwood then hand to Samira for technical details.
[00:00:28] Priya (CTO): Thanks Alex. We're excited to talk — Lighthouse Orbit is an integrator for enterprise SaaS to on-prem customers, lots of regulated customers in finance and healthcare.
[00:00:44] Marcus (Infra): Yup, we run a combination of cloud + on-prem GPU farms, and we need a clean onramp model for customers who want Redwood-hosted but with private networking.
[00:01:05] Alex (AE): Great, that maps pretty well to Redwood Dedicated and Private. Samira, want to frame our technical options?
[00:01:18] Samira (SE): Yeah. Quick overview: Redwood has three serving modes — hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC or on-prem). For integrators you typically pick Private with a customer-managed control plane or a VPC onramp that we federate to. We support KMS integrations, audit logs, and RBAC out of the box, though there are some nuances with air-gapped environments.
[00:01:45] Aisha (Partnerships): When you say "federate to" do you mean you run a control plane or we do? Some integrators want no control plane touching customer networks.
[00:02:00] Samira (SE): There are two patterns — 1) Redwood private control plane deployed into your VPC so we manage the control plane but no data plane leaves the VPC, or 2) full on-prem package — we give an appliance/helm chart and you run both control and data plane. Which is more interesting?
[00:02:22] Priya (CTO): For our largest regulated customers it's the second one. They will not allow any outbound to Redwood. For smaller ones we can do VPC peering with strict egress.
[00:02:39] Marcus (Infra): To add, our customers often have NVidia A100/NVIDIA H100 clusters with Slurm or Kubernetes. They care about multi-tenant isolation and GVNIC for low latency between host and GPU.
[00:02:59] Samira (SE): Understood. Our runtime picks kernels and handles KV cache — sometimes folks call it KV cash in docs — anyway we support multiple backends. We also have options for quantized model variants to lower GPU memory.
[00:03:17] Tom (Procurement): Quick question on contracts — what's typical pilot length, and do you require enterprise SLA for a pilot?
[00:03:31] Alex (AE): We usually do a 90-day pilot for Dedicated/Private pilots: baseline throughput, two-week perf runs, then a 60-day evaluation. For procurement we can do a limited SOW and a pilot addendum, no SLA until a committed contract.
[00:03:46] Priya (CTO): Okay we're trying to accelerate to a Q4 pilot with one anchor customer — timeline tight. We'll need security docs quickly.
[00:04:02] Alex (AE): We'll send SOC2, ISO attestation, and a security pack. Samira, I'll flag you to include SSO/SAML and KMS notes.
[00:04:14] Samira (SE): Absolutely. Also, note that when running fully on-prem our telemetry is optional. We can ship with local logs only for air-gapped setups.
[00:04:26] Marcus (Infra): That was one of our gating factors — telemetry only if customer signs off. On the networking side we need to understand how the model weights are distributed and any disk usage expectations. Some of our sites are constrained.
[00:04:43] Samira (SE): We can push model shards to customer storage or keep them local — deployment flavors vary. For H100s you'll typically use a 3-bit or 4-bit quantized variant to reduce memory; we can help recommend model + quant profile based on QPS and latency targets.
[00:04:59] Priya (CTO): Can you run benchmarks on our stack? We use K8s with GPU node pools and an internal LB.
[00:05:10] Samira (SE): Yes — we prepare a benchmark harness that runs generation and embedding QPS, measures p99 latency, and also exercises batching. It helps us pick kernel paths. We ask you for a sample prompt set and target latency/cost goals.
[00:05:30] Marcus (Infra): We'll share example prompt sets. On batching — a lot of our customers want low sub-200ms p95 for chat experiences, which limits batching window. How does Redwood balance batching vs latency?
[00:05:47] Samira (SE): We have an adaptive batching layer and policy rules. You can set hard latency SLOs which will bias to single-request fast lanes, while background throughput can be batched. There's also prefix/KV cache which we can lock to reduce repeated compute for similar prompts.
[00:06:05] Alex (AE): To hop in — that's actually a good place where Lighthouse can add value to customers: routing policy decisions and packaging caching layers in your connector.
[00:06:18] Aisha (Partnerships): Right, for integrators we can offer a marketplace connector that can be dropped into the customer cluster. It'll handle routing and credential exchange. We want to understand Redwood's expected interfaces.
[00:06:33] Samira (SE): Interfaces are standard REST + gRPC for high-throughput. For local on-prem we also offer a sidecar that speaks to the runtime — lightweight. For marketplace connector, you'll want to implement a small shim: auth, model selection, and fallback policy.
[00:06:51] Priya (CTO): About model selection — can the control plane route to smaller quantized variants automatically when capacity is low?
[00:07:03] Samira (SE): Yes, Smart routing is policy-driven. You can route by latency tier, cost tier, or model family. We also have canary rollouts and automatic fallback to compatible variants.
[00:07:20] Marcus (Infra): On security: our customers need KMS integrations (they run HashiCorp Vault) and HSM in some cases. Do you support customer-managed keys?
[00:07:34] Samira (SE): We support vault integrations and can use customer-managed KMS. In private deployments, keys never leave the customer's KMS. For hosted we do a bring-your-own-key model for the encryption at rest.
[00:07:48] Tom (Procurement): Cost question — doing Dedicated vs Private, where are the major unit-cost multipliers? GPU time? Ops support?
[00:07:59] Alex (AE): It's primarily GPU hours and memory footprint (bigger model = more GPU memory, more cost), plus reserved capacity premiums for Dedicated. Private on-prem removes GPU cost from Redwood but introduces integration and support fees. We'll include a cost example in the pilot proposal.
[00:08:18] Priya (CTO): For pilot success, we care about throughput (embedding QPS baseline), p95 generation latency under 300ms for short prompts, and stability during a spike test.
[00:08:31] Samira (SE): That's helpful; we'll encode those as pilot metrics. Also, do you have a preferred observability stack? We can push traces to your existing datadog/elastic stack or keep in our console.
[00:08:45] Marcus (Infra): Datadog is fine. For some customers we need to keep logs for 13 months, but that may be an enterprise add-on.
[00:08:58] Alex (AE): We'll document retention/retention add-on options.
[00:09:07] Aisha (Partnerships): Quick note: business model expectations — Lighthouse gets a referral or reseller margin on Dedicated/reserved capacity, and for Private we prefer an integrator fee for deployment + maintenance.
[00:09:22] Alex (AE): That's normal — Redwood has channel programs and reseller margins. We'll share the partner program deck.
[00:09:31] Priya (CTO): One of our bigger customers does not allow outbound TLS to third parties. How have you handled fully air-gapped installs?
[00:09:45] Samira (SE): For fully air-gapped we provide an on-prem package, offline install bundle, and a local-only control plane. We have done that for federal and some health customers. It increases deployment complexity and support overhead — typically a professional services fee.
[00:10:03] Marcus (Infra): Can you give an example SLA for on-prem support? Some customers want 24x7 on-call.
[00:10:12] Alex (AE): We can do escalated enterprise-support tiers with 4-hour incident response and dedicated TAM. Those would be in the enterprise contract. For pilots it's usually business-hours support unless contracted.
[00:10:28] Priya (CTO): For the benchmark harness: can you exercise both generation and embeddings and also show cost per 1k tokens?
[00:10:40] Samira (SE): Yes. Our lab harness measures tokens, GPU utilization, per-token latency, and maps to an estimated cost given reserved vs bursty capacity. We'll show cost breakdown per 1k tokens and per embedding call.
[00:10:55] Marcus (Infra): Any known gotchas with multi-node KV cache? We often see cache coherency issues with long contexts.
[00:11:06] Samira (SE): We use a KV cache manager and can pin prefixes for stronger locality. It's not perfect — long sequential contexts do increase pressure and there's a tradeoff. We'll recommend eviction policies.
[00:11:19] Alex (AE): Switching topics briefly: integration cadence — do you want a technical deep dive next week or would you prefer security docs first?
[00:11:32] Priya (CTO): Security docs first — procurement wants SOC2 right away. After that schedule a 2-hour technical deep dive with Marcus and your SE.
[00:11:44] Tom (Procurement): We'll also need redwood's master services agreement draft to review for procurement timelines.
[00:11:52] Alex (AE): Noted. We'll send a redlined MSA template for pilots.
[00:11:58] Aisha (Partnerships): On marketplace connector packaging: what's the recommended distribution? Helm chart + images?
[00:12:08] Samira (SE): Helm chart + OCI images is what we recommend. We can provide a reference repo. For air-gapped installs, we provide tarballs.
[00:12:18] Priya (CTO): Great. One more item — do you have terraform providers to automate provisioning?
[00:12:27] Samira (SE): Yes, we have terraform modules for dedicated and VPC onramp flows. For on-prem there's a repo with charts and a small operator.
[00:12:36] Marcus (Infra): Good. For the benchmark we'll give you a shadow cluster to run tests — what do you need from us?
[00:12:44] Samira (SE): Node access, sample prompt sets, target SLOs, and a small credentials bucket for the harness. We'll share the checklist.
[00:12:54] Alex (AE): I'm going to recap the ask: Redwood to share SOC2/security pack, partner program deck, and an on-prem deployment playbook. Samira will own the benchmark harness. Lighthouse to share infra diagram and prompt sets. We'll schedule the 2h tech deep dive after security docs.
[00:13:12] Priya (CTO): Sounds good.
[00:13:17] -- Silence for ambient notes --
[00:14:05] Speaker 1 (misc): [inaudible]...
[00:16:30] Samira (SE): One more technical note — model loading: for very low-latency ties we can pre-warm KV caches and pre-load weights into GPU memory, but that costs memory and some orchestration complexity.
[00:20:00] Marcus (Infra): Would Redwood's runtime support side-by-side inference with Triton? Some customers already use Triton in production.
[00:20:18] Samira (SE): We can interop at the RPC layer. If you want to keep Triton for some models that's possible, though you'll lose some of our smart-routing benefits.
[00:24:01] Priya (CTO): Can you give an example of a fallback policy? E.g., if H100 pool is saturated do you route to a quantized H100 or a lower-spec GPU?
[00:24:18] Samira (SE): Yes, fallback can be configured: same model quantized on same hardware, or route to a cheaper instance in another region, or fallback to embeddings-only for a degraded experience. Policy syntax is YAML based.
[00:29:05] Alex (AE): Any blockers from Lighthouse side for moving to pilot?
[00:29:13] Priya (CTO): We'll need internal legal sign off and proof of concept acceptance criteria. Also want to confirm telemetry opt-out for some customers.
[00:29:27] Tom (Procurement): Legal will need the MSA, data processing addendum, and proof that keys are customer-managed.
[00:29:38] Alex (AE): We'll include those documents.
[00:29:45] Marcus (Infra): Performance: would you consider a hybrid approach where inference runs locally but model updates are pushed from Redwood?
[00:29:58] Samira (SE): Yes — model distribution with signed artifacts is something we do. Updates can be pushed via your operator and validated with checksums; that's a standard process for on-prem.
[00:30:14] Aisha (Partnerships): Partner economics: does Redwood co-sell or is it strictly referral?
[00:30:25] Alex (AE): We can do both; depends on the contract. We have a co-sell program for strategic partners and a reseller margin for others. We'll share the partner program slide.
[00:30:40] Priya (CTO): Ok, how about timing? We want a pilot to start mid-Oct. Is that realistic?
[00:30:50] Samira (SE): If you can share the infra diagram and access by Oct 6, we can run an initial lab by Oct 11 and start the pilot mid-Oct. Tight but feasible.
[00:31:05] Alex (AE): I'll mark action items and follow up via email with the links.
[00:31:15] -- Background chatter; people joining/leaving --
[00:34:02] Marcus (Infra): On monitoring, how do token-level cost reports look? We'd like a per-route cost breakdown.
[00:34:15] Samira (SE): Our console provides token-level breakdown and cost per route, plus token-level traces if you enable it. For private installs we can export the same metrics to your monitoring stack.
[00:38:00] Priya (CTO): Any red flags with customers that run strict latency SLAs?
[00:38:12] Samira (SE): Main things are cold-starts and KV cache pressure. Pre-warming and pinned models help. Also for extremely low-latency needs we recommend reserving dedicated GPU capacity.
[00:42:00] Tom (Procurement): From procurement: are there any mandatory insurance or compliance items for pilots?
[00:42:12] Alex (AE): We'll include a standard pilot SOW; insurance is normally per enterprise deal. For pilots our legal team can be flexible.
[00:46:30] Aisha (Partnerships): One tactical ask: we'd like a reference architecture doc for a marketplace connector that integrates Redwood with our orchestration.
[00:46:42] Samira (SE): We'll produce a reference arch doc and a starter repo with helm charts.
[00:49:00] Priya (CTO): For resource planning: what on-call footprint does Redwood expect during pilot?
[00:49:12] Alex (AE): For pilots, we provide core hours support plus an on-call rotation for critical incidents. If you need 24/7 we'll propose an enterprise support add-on.
[00:52:10] Marcus (Infra): Last technical question: does Redwood's runtime allow pluggable scheduling for GPU-bound inference jobs?
[00:52:22] Samira (SE): Yes, we expose scheduling knobs. For Kubernetes we provide an operator that sets node affinities and allocates GPU slices.
[00:55:00] Alex (AE): Okay, quick recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2/security pack, partner deck, MSA template, and the on-prem playbook. Samira will prepare the benchmark harness and checklist. Lighthouse to send infra diagram and prompt samples. We agreed to try to schedule a 2h technical deep dive the week of Oct 11.
[00:55:28] Priya (CTO): That works for us. Thanks everyone.
[00:55:33] Tom (Procurement): Thanks.
[00:55:36] Samira (SE): Thanks, bye.
[00:55:40] Alex (AE): Thanks all. Bye.
